svg.title: P-OPT columns and the LLC capacity budget
svg.desc: For full Twitter, one one-byte-per-property-line column is 2,603,265 bytes. Full P-OPT keeps two columns and SE keeps one, while both retain 256 backing columns. Sixteen-way bars show the full and single-epoch reservations at 8, 16 and 24 MiB. ECG's extra on-chip state is separately disclosed rather than compared to DRAM matrix storage as a silicon ratio.
svg.text: P-OPT columns and the LLC capacity budget
A resident epoch column is graph-sized. Two columns do not mean two cache ways.
BACKING MATRIX IS NOT ALL IN THE LLC
column bytes = ceil(vertices x 4 / 64) = 2,603,265; no fixed-way shortcut.
One-column residency does not halve the 256-column stream over a complete traversal.
SE uses a different six-bit-value encoding. A two-way undercharge of full P-OPT is not SE.
separate data capacity, on-chip state and backing storage
At 8 MiB: Scale6 retains 16 data ways and adds about 560 KiB of line/controller state.
That is not yet an equal-area comparison. Total metadata-footprint ratios are not silicon-area ratios.
The two SE post-final interpretations are disclosed reconstructions, not bit-exact paper reproductions.
